standard_prerequisites.name: Hook Schur function
standard_prerequisites.statement: s_{N-k,1^k} is the Schur function of the hook shape with k boxes below the first row.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the shape appearing in the claimed expansion.

standard_prerequisites.name: Descent set of a hook tableau
standard_prerequisites.statement: Every standard Young tableau of hook shape (N-k,1^k) has exactly k descents, and each k-subset of [N-1] arises from exactly one such tableau.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the bijective step in the forward direction at source line 1344.

standard_prerequisites.name: Schur-positivity criterion
standard_prerequisites.statement: A set is symmetric for D if and only if its generating function expands over standard Young tableaux with coefficients depending only on the shape.
standard_prerequisites.use: It converts the displayed generating-function identity into the Schur expansion at source line 1349.

core_obligations: Assume first that |A(D = J)| = c_{|J|} for all J and note that hook tableaux have exactly k descents and that every k-subset arises from exactly one hook tableau (source line 1344).
Conclude that the generating function of A equals the sum over k of c_k times the sum over hook tableaux of t^{Des(T)}, which is the required shape (source lines 1345-1348).
Apply the retained Schur-positivity criterion to convert that identity into the claimed expansion with c_k = |A(D = [k])| (source line 1349).

For the converse, assume the hook expansion and use that a generating function determines its descent-set distribution, which gives |A(D = J)| = c_{|J|} and identifies c_k with the count on [k] (source line 1351).

proof_roadmap.step: Forward direction: hook tableaux and their descent sets.
Rewrite the generating function and apply the Schur-positivity criterion.
Converse direction from uniqueness of the descent-set distribution.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled proposition `prop:hook schur positive` at source lines 1334-1341: a set A has a hook-shaped non-negative Schur expansion if and only if the number |A(D = J)| depends only on |J|, with c_k the count on [k]. The author's proof (source lines 1343-1352) has two directions of different character. The forward direction is a bijective computation: it uses that a hook tableau of shape (N-k,1^k) has exactly k descents and that each k-subset arises from exactly one hook tableau (line 1344), which turns the uniform hypothesis into the displayed generating-function identity (lines 1345-1348) before the Schur-positivity criterion is applied (line 1349). The converse is not a computation at all: it rests on the uniqueness of the descent-set distribution of a generating function, cited from Adin and Roichman at line 1351. The statement is a two-way equivalence whose two halves are proved by completely different means.
